text:
Corey Perry is 41, back with Los Angeles for a second run, and still scoring the kind of goal he's scored for two decades: batted out of the air in front, against Pittsburgh on Saturday. He has two goals in his last four games after none in his first nine.

The Kings use him in short bursts, about 13 minutes a night, though he played 18 and 20 when they needed bodies against Ottawa and Buffalo. Los Angeles has 54% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and it has scored 2.7 fewer goals than those chances deserve. His own two goals came on 3.5 expected.

Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, most of it on the power play, while noting his results ran ahead of his chances. He has a Hart Trophy, a Rocket Richard and a Stanley Cup from 2007, and he's past 1,470 career games. Our projection sees about 17 goals.
